actual.transcript:
Morning everyone, let's run through the board. Priya, anything urgent before we start?
Nothing urgent. The team is happy with the explore experience so far, we just need the usage events data in.
Great. Theo, where are we on the usage events model?
I looked at the volumes — about forty million rows a day — so a full refresh is off the table. It needs to be incremental, partitioned by event date.
That matches what we do elsewhere in the project. Do you want to write that config or should we?
I'll take it. I'll draft the incremental model config for the usage events table and have it in a PR by Thursday the 18th.
Perfect, I'll review it same day.
Next blocker: the connection from our cloud is still being refused by your warehouse. Jonas, that's the network policy, right?
Yes, it's on me. I'll add the Quarry static IPs to our warehouse network policy — I can get that done by end of day Wednesday, June 17th.
That unblocks the scheduled refreshes, thank you. Priya, last one is pilot scope.
Right. I have a shortlist of six dashboards but I want the analytics guild to agree on which four make the pilot. I'll circulate the pilot dashboard list to the analytics guild and get sign-off by Friday the 19th.
Six to four sounds right for a pilot.
One more thing — at some point we should think about row-level security for the sales team, but that's not a today problem.
Agreed, let's park row-level security until after the pilot. Anything else?
Nope, all clear on our side.
Great, short and sharp. Talk next Monday.

actual.transcript:
Thanks for making time, both. The goal today is to get the security review moving again — it's been the blocker for three weeks.
Honest answer from our side: the review is stuck because we're missing two inputs — your completed SIG Lite questionnaire and evidence from a recent penetration test. Handling patient lab results, our infosec team can't wave either through.
The questionnaire is ninety percent done, our security lead has the last section. I'll send the completed SIG Lite questionnaire back to Freya by June 5th.
Friday works. If I have it Friday, I can start the internal review the following week.
And the pen test — we have the Q1 report from our external testers. Do you need the full report or a summary?
A summary with scope and findings severity is enough. Actually, easier if it lives with the rest of the evidence — I'll get the pen test summary uploaded to your portal by Monday, June 8th, once Sam shares it.
I'll email it to you right after this call, it's ready to go.
Then the last link in the chain is me. The warehouse team won't create the service account until security signs off — and with PHI in the schema they're strict about it.
Can we pre-agree the shape so it's a same-day job once you get the green light?
Yes — read-only, scoped to the ANALYTICS schema, key-pair auth. I'll provision the read-only Snowflake service account as soon as security signs off — targeting Wednesday, June 10th.
That's realistic if the questionnaire lands Friday.
Do we need your change advisory board for the account creation? That added two weeks last time at another customer.
No — we agreed internally last month that read-only analytics accounts skip the change board. It goes straight through.
Excellent. So: questionnaire Friday the 5th, pen test summary Monday the 8th, service account Wednesday the 10th. That's the chain unblocked.
Agreed. Nice to have dates on it at last.
Thanks all — I'll recap in the portal after this.

actual.transcript:
Hi both — today is all embedded analytics. Elise, want to restate the goal so we're aligned?
Sure. We want each of our recruiting customers to see their own dashboards inside our product — their pipeline, their time-to-hire, nobody else's. Tenant isolation is non-negotiable.
Understood. The right pattern here is signed JWTs: your backend mints a short-lived token per user, the token carries the tenant identity, and the embed respects it.
That works for us — we already issue session tokens, we'd just extend the claims.
Good. Let's make it concrete. Theo, can you stand up a sandbox they can develop against?
Yes — I'll set up the embed sandbox with signed JWT auth and share credentials by Wednesday, June 24th.
Then the ball is with me. I'll expose the customer_id claim in our session token — deployed to staging by Friday, June 26th.
One question — how does the customer_id claim actually filter the data? Is that per dashboard or global?
Global, enforced at the semantic layer, so a dashboard can't accidentally leak across tenants. I'll write up the row-level filtering approach for multi-tenant embeds and send it over by Thursday the 25th.
Great, I'd like our security folks to read that before we go further.
Sensible. The write-up plus the sandbox should give them everything they need to poke at it.
It might be worth load-testing the embeds eventually, but let's see it working first.
Agreed — load testing is a later conversation. So: sandbox Wednesday, write-up Thursday, staging claim Friday. Reconvene next Monday?
Works for us. Thanks both.

actual.transcript:
Sharing my screen — this is your fct_returns model compiled in our dev project. Let's define the first metrics on top of it.
The two the leadership team asks for every week are return rate and total refund value. If those two are self-serve we've already won.
Then those are our first metrics block. return_rate as returned orders over total orders, refund_total as a simple sum — both defined in the .yml, next to the model.
I want to write that myself so the team learns the workflow. I'll add the metrics block to fct_returns.yml — return_rate and refund_total — and open the PR by Monday, June 1st.
Perfect. And I'll review the PR and validate the compiled SQL in the dev project by Tuesday, June 2nd, so we catch any grain mistakes before anyone builds on it.
One data issue before you trust return_rate — exchange_type is null for everything before March. Exchanges will be undercounted.
Good catch. Do we coalesce in the metric or fix the staging model?
Fix it at the source — the mapping exists in the raw events, it just predates the column. I'll backfill the exchange_type column in the staging model by end of week — Friday, May 29th.
That's cleaner. Then my PR can assume exchange_type is trustworthy.
Agreed — Dev's backfill lands first, then the metrics PR. Anything else while we're in the model?
Eventually we'll want a returns-by-reason breakdown, but I don't want to scope that today.
Noted for later, not committing to it now. Good session — recap coming your way.
Thanks Theo, this was useful.

Done. So: comments Friday, pilot list Monday, dashboard Wednesday. Talk next week.
Thanks Ines.

That's what I'm hoping. We've lost about three weeks; if the connection happens next week we can claw most of that back.
From my side, no further reviews needed after this one. The tool itself was approved — it was the data-sharing terms for the health data that took time.
Good to know. I won't pile more actions on — the sign-off and the service account are the whole critical path. Anything you need from me?
Nothing right now. If provisioning throws anything weird I'll ping you on Slack.
Perfect. Let's speak once the account is live. Thanks both.

Thanks Maya. Sorry the project went dark for three weeks, that was me, not the team losing interest.
No apology needed. Let's rebuild the picture — where do things actually stand?
Better than you'd think. IT finished the Okta SAML SSO configuration while I was out — it's done, tested, people log in through Okta now.
Excellent, I'll stop chasing that one. The other open item on my board is the metric definitions.
Yeah, that one's still on me and still not started. We still owe you the metric definitions — I'll get the first ten drafted in the yml now that I'm back.
Good. Given the gap, I don't want to pretend the old dates still hold.
Agreed, chasing the original timeline would just stress everyone out.
Then I'll re-baseline the implementation timeline and send you the updated plan by Thursday.
Perfect. One more thing from our side — your team asked what fields we track per shipment.
Yes, we need that to model the shipment marts properly.
I'll deliver the shipment data dictionary by end of next week — it exists, it just needs cleaning up before I share it.
That unblocks the modeling work nicely. Anything else in flight I should know about?
There's vague talk of a carrier-scorecard module on our roadmap that might want dashboards, but it's a quarter away at least.
Noted for later, not for the plan. Great to have you back, Owen.
Good to be back. Talk Thursday when the plan lands.

Hi Tessa — week two! Last week ended with the warehouse connection half done. Where did it land?
Landed well. We got the BigQuery connection working on Tuesday — Quarry reads from the analytics dataset without a hitch. Mark it done.
Great start. Next decision is where to begin modeling — you mentioned the newsletter-engagement data is your cleanest.
By far. The ad-revenue tables are a mess of legacy columns; sends and opens are what the growth team actually asks about daily.
Then we start with the newsletter-engagement marts. I'll fold that into a tailored onboarding plan and share it with you on Monday.
Perfect. What do you need from us to keep pace?
Mainly your analysts in the workspace early, so they learn the tool while we build rather than after.
Makes sense. I'll invite our two analysts to the workspace by Wednesday — they're excited to poke around anyway.
That's exactly the energy we want in week two.
Longer term we'd love ad-revenue attribution out of this too — sponsorship performance and so on — but I know that's a later phase.
It is, and it'll be a good one. I'll note it for the roadmap conversation, nothing to do now.
Great. So plan from you Monday, invites from me by Wednesday.
Exactly. Enjoy the long weekend, Tessa.
